icml-2017-convolutional-sequence-to-sequ.problem: Translation systems must turn an input sentence into an output of variable length, but recurrent networks process the sequence in a way that limits parallel training.
icml-2017-convolutional-sequence-to-sequ.idea: Replace recurrence with convolutions, use gates to help gradients flow, and give every decoder layer its own attention mechanism for consulting the input.
icml-2017-convolutional-sequence-to-sequ.results: The model exceeds the reported accuracy of a deep LSTM baseline on WMT 2014 English–German and English–French translation, with roughly an order-of-magnitude speed advantage on CPU and GPU.
icml-2017-convolutional-sequence-to-sequ.limitations: The abstract establishes results on two translation benchmarks; it does not give absolute quality scores, model sizes, or a breakdown of training versus inference timing.
icml-2017-convolutional-sequence-to-sequ.tldr: A fully convolutional sequence model improves translation accuracy while making computation substantially faster than the compared recurrent model.

icml-2017-high-dimensional-structured-qu.problem: Quantile regression predicts a response's median or other quantiles, but estimation becomes difficult when there are more predictors than observations.
icml-2017-high-dimensional-structured-qu.idea: Assume the true coefficient vector has exploitable structure, express that structure through an atomic norm, and penalize the estimator with that norm.
icml-2017-high-dimensional-structured-qu.results: The analysis gives sample requirements for consistent recovery and finite-sample error bounds, exposing geometric and statistical features of the problem; synthetic experiments support the theory.
icml-2017-high-dimensional-structured-qu.limitations: The guarantees depend on the assumed low-complexity parameter structure. The abstract does not specify the full statistical assumptions or report tests on real datasets.
icml-2017-high-dimensional-structured-qu.tldr: Structured regularization makes high-dimensional quantile estimation analyzable through explicit sample and error bounds.

icml-2017-multiple-clustering-views-from.problem: Different experts may reasonably group the same data in different ways, while existing approaches often compress their uncertain advice into a single clustering.
icml-2017-multiple-clustering-views-from.idea: Jointly infer multiple expert viewpoints, a clustering for each viewpoint, and expert confidence using a Bayesian model and variational inference.
icml-2017-multiple-clustering-views-from.results: Experiments on synthetic data, benchmarks, and disease subtyping report better performance than several clustering baselines, with confidence estimates used to weight expert contributions.
icml-2017-multiple-clustering-views-from.limitations: The abstract does not describe how expert feedback is encoded, how many viewpoints are recovered, or the size of the improvements; these details matter when applying the method to a new group of experts.
icml-2017-multiple-clustering-views-from.tldr: A Bayesian clustering model preserves multiple expert perspectives instead of forcing every expert into one consensus grouping.

icml-2018-canonical-tensor-decomposition.problem: A knowledge base can be viewed as a three-dimensional table of entity–relation facts, yet a natural low-rank factorization of that table has lagged behind competing completion methods.
icml-2018-canonical-tensor-decomposition.idea: Improve canonical tensor decomposition with a tensor-norm regularizer and a formulation that treats relations and their inverses consistently.
icml-2018-canonical-tensor-decomposition.results: Together, the changes outperform the then-current state of the art on several datasets using canonical decomposition, and improve the more expressive ComplEx model further.
icml-2018-canonical-tensor-decomposition.limitations: The abstract does not name the evaluated datasets or provide numerical gains, and it does not establish how the method performs on relations unlike those in the benchmarks.
icml-2018-canonical-tensor-decomposition.tldr: Better regularization and consistent handling of inverse relations make a simple tensor model competitive for predicting missing knowledge-base facts.

icml-2018-communication-computation-effi.problem: Distributed gradient computation can be slowed by lagging workers, excessive duplicated work, or communication overhead; optimizing only one of these costs can miss the best overall design.
icml-2018-communication-computation-effi.idea: Characterize their joint tradeoff and construct polynomial-based codes that combine information across both data subsets and gradient-vector components.
icml-2018-communication-computation-effi.results: The coding scheme reaches the stated optimal tradeoff. EC2 experiments report unchanged generalization error and runtime reductions of 32% versus uncoded schemes and 23% versus earlier straggler-focused codes.
icml-2018-communication-computation-effi.limitations: The abstract does not describe the cluster scale, workloads, or networking conditions behind the timing gains; the theoretical optimum is for the modeled tradeoff.
icml-2018-communication-computation-effi.tldr: Gradient coding can balance redundancy, slow-worker tolerance, and communication to shorten distributed training computations.

icml-2018-high-performance-zero-memory-o.problem: Fast convolution implementations often allocate extra working memory, limiting the networks that fit on small devices and potentially leaving CPU performance untapped.
icml-2018-high-performance-zero-memory-o.idea: Implement convolution directly, avoiding the packing or auxiliary storage required by alternative high-performance routines.
icml-2018-high-performance-zero-memory-o.results: The authors report eliminating additional memory overhead, improving performance by 10% to 400% over compared implementations on conventional and embedded CPUs, and scaling better as thread count increases.
icml-2018-high-performance-zero-memory-o.limitations: The abstract does not list the convolution shapes, processor models, or baseline configurations, so the reported speed range should not be assumed for every layer or device.
icml-2018-high-performance-zero-memory-o.tldr: Carefully engineered direct convolution can save working memory while outperforming existing CPU convolution routines.

icml-2018-to-understand-deep-learning-we.problem: Deep networks can fit their training data perfectly and still generalize well, challenging familiar explanations that equate exact fitting with poor test performance.
icml-2018-to-understand-deep-learning-we.idea: Study the same phenomenon in simpler kernel machines through experiments and bounds on the norm of interpolating solutions.
icml-2018-to-understand-deep-learning-we.results: Kernel interpolators perform well on six real and two synthetic datasets. Smooth-kernel solution norms can grow nearly exponentially with dataset size, and existing bounds fail to explain these solutions; Laplacian kernels also readily fit random labels.
icml-2018-to-understand-deep-learning-we.limitations: The work demonstrates parallels and shortcomings in existing theory rather than supplying a complete explanation of deep-network generalization. The abstract's connection to kernel properties is an experimentally motivated interpretation.
icml-2018-to-understand-deep-learning-we.tldr: Kernel methods also generalize after exact fitting, making them a useful testing ground for understanding overparameterized learning.

icml-2019-discriminative-regularization-.problem: A generative model can overlook a subtle signal that predicts an important outcome because that signal explains only a small share of overall data variation.
icml-2019-discriminative-regularization-.idea: Use a black-box predictor to regularize latent-variable training so the learned representation retains variation relevant to that predictor, then visualize and measure it.
icml-2019-discriminative-regularization-.results: The approach is evaluated with synthetic and real electrocardiogram data, statistical summaries, and a physician experiment to study variation influencing clinically relevant predictions.
icml-2019-discriminative-regularization-.limitations: The abstract provides no numerical accuracy or interpretability results, and does not establish that the highlighted predictive variation is causal or sufficient for clinical use.
icml-2019-discriminative-regularization-.tldr: A predictive model can guide a generative representation toward the subtle features that matter for its decisions.

icml-2019-multiplicative-weights-updates.problem: Guarantees that first-order optimization avoids problematic saddle points often exclude constrained solutions on the boundary, leaving an important class of applications uncovered.
icml-2019-multiplicative-weights-updates.idea: Analyze a multiplicative-weights update for smooth non-concave objectives over products of simplices, combining dynamical-systems arguments with a related polynomial inequality.
icml-2019-multiplicative-weights-updates.results: For sufficiently small steps, the update almost always converges to critical points satisfying second-order Karush–Kuhn–Tucker conditions.
icml-2019-multiplicative-weights-updates.limitations: The result concerns a specific feasible-set structure and smoothness regime. Second-order stationarity does not establish a globally optimal solution, and the abstract gives no practical convergence-rate bound.
icml-2019-multiplicative-weights-updates.tldr: Multiplicative weights gains a second-order convergence guarantee for a class of constrained non-concave optimization problems.

icml-2019-sparse-extreme-multi-label-lea.problem: Sparse local embeddings are promising for prediction with extremely many labels, but their statistical convergence and ability to recover the relevant underlying model have lacked a clear account.
icml-2019-sparse-extreme-multi-label-lea.idea: Place sparse local embedding estimation in a framework with a nonconvex penalty and analyze the resulting estimator.
icml-2019-sparse-extreme-multi-label-lea.results: The estimator has an oracle property and a stated statistical convergence rate, with a faster rate under an additional condition on underlying parameter magnitudes; numerical experiments support the analysis.
icml-2019-sparse-extreme-multi-label-lea.limitations: The abstract does not give the rate formulas or the complete assumptions needed for the oracle guarantee, and it does not quantify the experimental advantage.
icml-2019-sparse-extreme-multi-label-lea.tldr: A nonconvex sparse-embedding estimator comes with statistical guarantees for extreme multi-label prediction.

icml-2020-automated-synthetic-to-real-ge.problem: A model trained on synthetic images can lose useful real-image knowledge inherited from ImageNet, hurting transfer to real data and requiring laborious learning-rate tuning.
icml-2020-automated-synthetic-to-real-ge.idea: Encourage the model to preserve representations similar to its ImageNet-pretrained starting point, while learning to choose learning rates separately for different layers.
icml-2020-automated-synthetic-to-real-ge.results: The framework improves synthetic-to-real generalization without training on real target data and also benefits downstream domain adaptation.
icml-2020-automated-synthetic-to-real-ge.limitations: The abstract reports no numerical gains or dataset-specific results. Its no-real-data claim concerns target training data, while the approach explicitly relies on ImageNet pretraining.
icml-2020-automated-synthetic-to-real-ge.tldr: Preserving pretrained representations and learning layer-specific update rates improves transfer from synthetic images to real ones.

icml-2020-information-particle-filter-tr.problem: An agent acting under partial observation may need to gather information before it can choose a useful action, especially in continuous environments.
icml-2020-information-particle-filter-tr.idea: Search over possible belief states with Monte Carlo tree search and particle-based simulations, adding expected information gain to the task reward.
icml-2020-information-particle-filter-tr.results: The proposed Information Particle Filter Tree algorithm improves performance on evaluated problems where gathering information is essential to an effective policy.
icml-2020-information-particle-filter-tr.limitations: The abstract does not identify benchmark sizes, runtime costs, or how the information-reward weight is chosen; it does not claim equal benefit when information gathering is unimportant.
icml-2020-information-particle-filter-tr.tldr: A particle-based planning tree explicitly values information to improve decisions under uncertainty.

icml-2020-online-continual-learning-from.problem: Continual learners must remember old classes while receiving correlated, uneven streams of new examples, but evaluations often assume balanced data.
icml-2020-online-continual-learning-from.idea: Introduce class-balancing reservoir sampling to choose which past examples occupy the learner's limited replay memory.
icml-2020-online-continual-learning-from.results: The proposed memory strategy outperforms compared state-of-the-art memory population methods across multiple datasets and architectures in a challenging imbalanced online setting.
icml-2020-online-continual-learning-from.limitations: The abstract omits memory budgets, imbalance severity, and numerical gains, so it does not establish how much replay storage is needed for a particular deployment.
icml-2020-online-continual-learning-from.tldr: Keeping a more class-balanced replay memory helps continual learners cope with imbalanced data streams.

icml-2020-optimal-sequential-maximizatio.problem: Selecting the strongest candidate from noisy question responses can require repeatedly revisiting candidates, which is awkward when items arrive in a stream.
icml-2020-optimal-sequential-maximizatio.idea: Develop a sequential selection algorithm that asks each candidate questions during one visit and never returns to a previously considered candidate.
icml-2020-optimal-sequential-maximizatio.results: The algorithm achieves optimal linear query complexity and the same order of selection accuracy as approaches that revisit candidates, with guarantees that also allow an unknown or infinite number of items.
icml-2020-optimal-sequential-maximizatio.limitations: The claims hold in the paper's probabilistic query model. The abstract does not state the precise confidence parameters or assumptions on candidate response probabilities.
icml-2020-optimal-sequential-maximizatio.tldr: Under a probabilistic selection model, one sequential interview per candidate is enough to achieve optimal-order query efficiency.

icml-2020-self-attentive-hawkes-process-.problem: Predicting the type and timing of future events requires understanding event history, including the uneven gaps that ordinary sequence-position encodings ignore.
icml-2020-self-attentive-hawkes-process-.idea: Build a Hawkes-process model around self-attention and encode elapsed time through phase shifts in sinusoidal functions.
icml-2020-self-attentive-hawkes-process-.results: Experiments report improved fit and event prediction. Attention weights also expose contributions between event types, providing a proposed route to interpreting the model.
icml-2020-self-attentive-hawkes-process-.limitations: The abstract provides no numerical comparisons or dataset descriptions; attention weights indicate model attribution here and do not establish causal influences between real events.
icml-2020-self-attentive-hawkes-process-.tldr: Time-aware self-attention improves a point-process model's use of irregular event histories.

icml-2020-sub-goal-trees-a-framework-for.problem: Goal-directed control needs a route between arbitrary start and goal states, while standard reinforcement learning naturally organizes decisions one next step at a time.
icml-2020-sub-goal-trees-a-framework-for.idea: Use an all-pairs-shortest-path formulation to recursively predict intermediate goals, splitting a trajectory into a tree of smaller subproblems.
icml-2020-sub-goal-trees-a-framework-for.results: The formulation offers computational benefits for exact and approximate dynamic programming and supports new policy-gradient algorithms; neural planning experiments improve navigation of a seven-degree-of-freedom robot arm around obstacles.
icml-2020-sub-goal-trees-a-framework-for.limitations: The abstract does not quantify computational savings or robot success rates, and the reported application does not establish performance across other control domains.
icml-2020-sub-goal-trees-a-framework-for.tldr: Building trajectories by recursively choosing intermediate goals creates a useful alternative to step-by-step goal-conditioned control.

icml-2021-best-model-identification-a-re.problem: Choosing the best learning algorithm is complicated when every trial also trains that algorithm, changing its future performance.
icml-2021-best-model-identification-a-re.idea: Model algorithms as rested bandit arms whose expected losses improve with use, assume a shared loss-curve family, and progressively eliminate weaker arms.
icml-2021-best-model-identification-a-re.results: The analyzed algorithm's regret vanishes as the available horizon grows; the convergence rate depends on the loss-curve form, and lower bounds clarify the solution's limits.
icml-2021-best-model-identification-a-re.limitations: The analysis assumes the expected loss curves are known up to parameters and share a similar shape; the abstract does not show robustness to misspecified learning curves.
icml-2021-best-model-identification-a-re.tldr: Best-model selection can be analyzed as a bandit problem in which testing an algorithm also improves it.

icml-2021-connecting-sphere-manifolds-hi.problem: A classifier trained on hierarchically related categories can benefit from expressing the relationship between a broad class and its more specific subclasses.
icml-2021-connecting-sphere-manifolds-hi.idea: Constrain each class's classifier to a sphere centered on its parent classifier, connect these spheres along the hierarchy, and replace the network's final classification layer accordingly.
icml-2021-connecting-sphere-manifolds-hi.results: This regularization improves ResNet and DenseNet performance on CIFAR100, CUB200, Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars, and Tiny ImageNet.
icml-2021-connecting-sphere-manifolds-hi.limitations: The method requires a class hierarchy. The abstract gives no improvement magnitudes or evidence about sensitivity to an inaccurate or incomplete hierarchy.
icml-2021-connecting-sphere-manifolds-hi.tldr: A hierarchy of spherical constraints encourages related classes to share structure in a neural classifier.

icml-2021-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.problem: Discovering an equation from observed input–output pairs is traditionally driven by hand-designed search procedures that do not learn from previous problems.
icml-2021-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.idea: Generate equations procedurally, pretrain a Transformer to infer symbolic formulas from their sampled values, and use its predictions to guide equation search on new data.
icml-2021-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.results: Experiments recover a collection of well-known physical equations, and performance improves with increased training data and compute.
icml-2021-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.limitations: The abstract does not specify the equation families, noise levels, or out-of-distribution tests, so recovery of these examples does not establish unrestricted scientific discovery.
icml-2021-neural-symbolic-regression-tha.tldr: Large-scale pretraining teaches a Transformer useful equation-search instincts for symbolic regression.

icml-2021-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.problem: An online ranking system must choose which items occupy limited display positions while learning how those choices affect user clicks.
icml-2021-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.idea: GRAB learns both the ranking and a compact graph connecting item permutations, exploiting a structure in which rewards improve toward a best ranking on that graph.
icml-2021-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.results: Under the position-based click model, the algorithm has a logarithmic regret bound. Simulated and real-data experiments report greater efficiency with regret comparable to the strongest compared methods.
icml-2021-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.limitations: The guarantee relies on the position-based model and the associated unimodality property. The abstract does not quantify efficiency gains or evaluate other click-behavior models.
icml-2021-parametric-graph-for-unimodal-.tldr: Learning a structured graph of rankings enables efficient online item placement with a logarithmic regret guarantee.

icml-2021-regularized-submodular-maximiz.problem: Selecting a small representative or diverse subset often requires balancing a submodular benefit against a cost, producing an objective that can be negative and evade standard guarantees.
icml-2021-regularized-submodular-maximiz.idea: Develop streaming and distributed algorithms for a monotone submodular benefit minus a modular penalty under a size limit.
icml-2021-regularized-submodular-maximiz.results: The paper gives a one-pass streaming method and a distributed method using O(1/epsilon) MapReduce rounds, with improved memory and communication scaling even without a penalty; applications include data summarization and network coverage.
icml-2021-regularized-submodular-maximiz.limitations: The abstract does not provide the full approximation guarantees or numerical application results. Its guarantees concern the specified benefit-minus-cost objective and cardinality constraint.
icml-2021-regularized-submodular-maximiz.tldr: Scalable algorithms extend representative-subset selection to objectives that subtract explicit costs from coverage or diversity.

icml-2021-sample-optimal-pac-learning-of.problem: Learning a linear decision boundary from maliciously corrupted examples needs both tolerance to contamination and efficient use of training samples.
icml-2021-sample-optimal-pac-learning-of.idea: Reanalyze an existing localized learning algorithm using a matrix concentration bound for empirical covariance, then extend it to a stronger corruption model.
icml-2021-sample-optimal-pac-learning-of.results: Under an isotropic log-concave data distribution, the analysis improves the near-optimal sample bound from roughly quadratic to roughly linear in dimension, up to logarithmic factors, and obtains polynomial-time guarantees for nasty noise.
icml-2021-sample-optimal-pac-learning-of.limitations: The distributional assumption and homogeneous halfspace hypothesis class are central; the abstract does not imply the same robustness for arbitrary datasets or nonlinear models.
icml-2021-sample-optimal-pac-learning-of.tldr: Sharper analysis reduces the sample requirement for robust halfspace learning from roughly quadratic to roughly linear in dimension.

icml-2022-convergence-and-recovery-guara.problem: K-subspaces clusters points lying near different low-dimensional subspaces, but its convergence and ability to recover the correct grouping need theoretical justification.
icml-2022-convergence-and-recovery-guara.idea: Analyze the method near a correct clustering and design an inner-product thresholding spectral initializer that reaches this favorable neighborhood.
icml-2022-convergence-and-recovery-guara.results: For the stated semi-random union-of-subspaces model, the method converges superlinearly and recovers the clustering with high probability in order log-log N iterations; numerical experiments support the results.
icml-2022-convergence-and-recovery-guara.limitations: The guarantee depends on the data-generation model and a suitable initialization neighborhood, even though subspaces may overlap. The abstract does not establish comparable recovery under arbitrary noise or outliers.
icml-2022-convergence-and-recovery-guara.tldr: A spectral starting point enables fast, provable recovery for K-subspaces clustering under a structured sampling model.

icml-2022-optimal-algorithms-for-mean-es.problem: Locally private mean estimators can share the same asymptotic accuracy rate yet differ greatly in practice because of hidden constants.
icml-2022-optimal-algorithms-for-mean-es.idea: Optimize the randomization mechanism itself, using symmetry and a linear-program characterization to identify the least-variance member of a broad natural class.
icml-2022-optimal-algorithms-for-mean-es.results: Optimally tuned PrivUnit achieves the best variance within that class. A Gaussian-based variant retains the guarantees and makes exact error constants easier to analyze and estimate numerically.
icml-2022-optimal-algorithms-for-mean-es.limitations: The optimality claim is scoped to the studied class of randomizers for bounded vectors; the abstract does not supply the actual constants or a full empirical benchmark.
icml-2022-optimal-algorithms-for-mean-es.tldr: Optimizing privacy randomization constants yields sharper accuracy guarantees for locally private mean estimation.

icml-2022-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.problem: Training an out-of-distribution detector with auxiliary outliers raises a selection problem: the possible outlier pool is enormous, and many examples may be uninformative.
icml-2022-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.idea: Use posterior sampling to mine useful outliers and learn a compact boundary separating in-distribution examples from outsiders.
icml-2022-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.results: POEM reports state-of-the-art benchmark performance and relative FPR95 improvements of 42.0% on CIFAR-10 and 24.2% on CIFAR-100 over a greedy-sampling comparator, alongside theoretical analysis.
icml-2022-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.limitations: The abstract does not specify the auxiliary outlier sources or absolute false-positive rates, and benchmark improvements do not establish detection of every unfamiliar input.
icml-2022-poem-out-of-distribution-detec.tldr: Posterior-guided outlier selection makes auxiliary data more effective for training an out-of-distribution detector.

icml-2022-revisiting-online-submodular-m.problem: Worst-case guarantees for online decisions with submodular losses miss the easier structure of stable environments, while purely stochastic methods may be vulnerable to adversarial changes.
icml-2022-revisiting-online-submodular-m.idea: Construct algorithms for both full-information and bandit feedback that adapt their regret to the environment, including settings with stochastic losses and adversarial corruption.
icml-2022-revisiting-online-submodular-m.results: The methods attain gap-dependent logarithmic regret in stochastic environments while matching the quality of existing adversarial guarantees, with results also covering an intermediate corrupted-stochastic regime.
icml-2022-revisiting-online-submodular-m.limitations: The abstract does not state the exact gap dependence, corruption penalty, or computational cost, so practical performance cannot be inferred from the high-level regret claims alone.
icml-2022-revisiting-online-submodular-m.tldr: Adaptive submodular decision algorithms gain logarithmic regret in favorable environments without giving up adversarial robustness.

icml-2022-understanding-instance-level-i.problem: Group-level fairness metrics reveal disparities but do not identify which individual training examples most influence those disparities.
icml-2022-understanding-instance-level-i.idea: Extend influence-function analysis to fairness-constrained learning, obtaining a kernelized decomposition under stated assumptions and ranking examples by their influence on fairness.
icml-2022-understanding-instance-level-i.results: Experiments find that training on selected influential subsets reduces fairness violations, with an accompanying tradeoff in predictive accuracy.
icml-2022-understanding-instance-level-i.limitations: The decomposition requires assumptions not detailed in the abstract, and reducing the tested statistical fairness violations does not establish that all individual outcomes are fair.
icml-2022-understanding-instance-level-i.tldr: Fairness influence scores connect group-level constraints to individual training examples and expose an accuracy–fairness tradeoff.

icml-2023-how-powerful-are-shallow-neura.problem: Freezing randomly chosen hidden-layer weights simplifies training, but it is unclear when the remaining trainable output layer can approximate a target arbitrarily well.
icml-2023-how-powerful-are-shallow-neura.idea: Use ridgelet analysis, related to harmonic analysis, to study two-layer networks whose random hidden parameters occupy a bounded domain.
icml-2023-how-powerful-are-shallow-neura.results: The paper derives a nonzero approximation-error lower bound in the studied setting and supports it with simulations, showing that arbitrary random-weight distributions need not provide universal approximation.
icml-2023-how-powerful-are-shallow-neura.limitations: The result concerns bounded random hidden parameters in shallow networks; it does not rule out universal approximation with appropriately chosen distributions or fully trained hidden layers.
icml-2023-how-powerful-are-shallow-neura.tldr: Random features are not automatically universal: their distribution must be suited to the complexity of the target function.

icml-2023-on-the-initialization-of-graph.problem: Standard neural-network initialization rules ignore how graph structure and message passing change signal and gradient variance in graph neural networks.
icml-2023-on-the-initialization-of-graph.idea: Analyze forward and backward variance jointly with activation functions, hidden width, and graph propagation, then design the Virgo initialization to stabilize variance across layers.
icml-2023-on-the-initialization-of-graph.results: Across 15 datasets spanning node classification, link prediction, and graph classification, Virgo produces more stable initial variance and improved model performance.
icml-2023-on-the-initialization-of-graph.limitations: The abstract does not provide gain sizes, identify the graph architectures tested, or establish that initialization alone resolves other deep-GNN training difficulties.
icml-2023-on-the-initialization-of-graph.tldr: Graph-aware initialization improves the starting flow of signals and gradients through graph neural networks.

icml-2024-accelerating-pde-data-generati.problem: Neural PDE solvers can be fast after training, but producing their high-precision training examples is itself computationally expensive.
icml-2024-accelerating-pde-data-generati.idea: DiffOAS combines a small collection of base solutions and applies differential operators to the resulting functions to generate new PDE data efficiently.
icml-2024-accelerating-pde-data-generati.results: The analysis reports one-order-lower time complexity, while experiments generate 10,000-instance datasets up to 300 times faster; neural operators trained with 5% of the generation time achieve comparable performance.
icml-2024-accelerating-pde-data-generati.limitations: The abstract does not specify the PDE families, boundary conditions, or base-solution requirements, so the speedups should be read within the evaluated generation settings.
icml-2024-accelerating-pde-data-generati.tldr: Constructing solutions first and applying the differential operator can sharply reduce the cost of generating PDE training data.

icml-2024-beyond-the-calibration-point-m.problem: Two privacy mechanisms can share one reported epsilon–delta pair while having meaningfully different privacy behavior elsewhere, making single-point comparisons incomplete.
icml-2024-beyond-the-calibration-point-m.idea: Introduce a divergence that measures the worst-case extra privacy vulnerability of one mechanism relative to another, with several privacy interpretations and decision-theoretic foundations.
icml-2024-beyond-the-calibration-point-m.results: Application examples reveal gaps hidden by standard comparisons and show that common DP-SGD choices can have high excess privacy vulnerability by this measure.
icml-2024-beyond-the-calibration-point-m.limitations: The abstract does not list the mechanisms or numerical vulnerabilities in those examples. The comparison quantifies a relative risk criterion rather than declaring all mechanisms with matching privacy parameters equivalent.
icml-2024-beyond-the-calibration-point-m.tldr: A fuller comparison of privacy guarantees can reveal differences that a single epsilon–delta calibration point hides.

icml-2024-efficient-black-box-adversaria.problem: Black-box adversarial evaluation must find misleading inputs using only model outputs, and local gradient guidance from a surrogate can still require many queries.
icml-2024-efficient-black-box-adversaria.idea: Use the surrogate's loss as a global function prior for Bayesian optimization, then adapt the prior's influence using a regret-based criterion.
icml-2024-efficient-black-box-adversaria.results: Experiments on image classifiers and large vision-language models report fewer queries and higher attack success than compared state-of-the-art black-box methods.
icml-2024-efficient-black-box-adversaria.limitations: The analysis explicitly identifies poor priors as a possible problem. The abstract provides no query budgets or effect sizes, and the method assumes access to a useful surrogate model.
icml-2024-efficient-black-box-adversaria.tldr: An adaptively weighted surrogate-function prior improves query efficiency in black-box adversarial testing.

icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.problem: Long prompts delay an autoregressive language model's first output token, even though later tokens benefit from an existing key–value cache.
icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.idea: Parallelize prompt processing by coordinating multiple processes to fill the cache, and balance work across context segments to account for causal attention's uneven workload.
icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.results: KV-Runahead reports speedups above 1.4× for Llama 7B and 1.6× for Falcon 7B relative to compared parallelization schemes.
icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.limitations: The method targets the prompt phase and time to first token. The abstract does not establish corresponding improvements in later-token throughput or specify hardware and prompt lengths for the gains.
icml-2024-kv-runahead-scalable-causal-ll.tldr: Parallel key–value cache construction speeds up the first-token phase of causal language-model inference.

icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.problem: An explanation that selects features for one prediction can secretly encode extra information through the selection pattern, creating misleading apparent interpretability.
icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.idea: Formalize label and feature leakage, derive necessary and sufficient conditions for avoiding them, and design the SUWR selection method to satisfy those conditions.
icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.results: Existing methods fail the derived conditions, while SUWR has a no-leakage guarantee and experiments report strong predictive performance, sparse selections, and less tendency to overfit.
icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.limitations: The guarantee addresses the formalized leakage mechanisms; the abstract does not establish that every selected explanation is causally valid or understandable to every user.
icml-2024-local-feature-selection-withou.tldr: Leakage-free local feature selection makes sparse prediction explanations more reliable under an explicit mathematical definition.

icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.problem: Prediction intervals for a target population must remain reliable when available datasets come from biased sources and individual-level data sharing is constrained.
icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.idea: Use influence-function-based estimation of outcome quantiles and adapt source weights to favor informative datasets while reducing bias from incompatible sources.
icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.results: The analysis gives convergence to nominal coverage at parametric rates under its conditions; synthetic experiments and pediatric cardiac-surgery length-of-stay prediction illustrate robustness and efficiency.
icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.limitations: The abstract does not provide interval widths or subgroup coverage results, and the theoretical claims rely on assumptions about source–target relationships and nuisance estimation that are not fully stated here.
icml-2024-multi-source-conformal-inferen.tldr: Adaptive use of multiple data sources can improve prediction intervals while accounting for population shifts.

icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.problem: Comparing language models on average safety or reliability scores can hide differences in the distribution of undesirable outcomes and uncertainty in the comparison.
icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.idea: Use statistical tests of stochastic dominance and combine metrics into portfolios, borrowing risk–utility ideas from finance to guide model selection under specified guardrails.
icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.results: The paper develops asymptotic significance guarantees with bootstrap variance estimation and applies the framework to instruction drift and toxic outputs across language models.
icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.limitations: The abstract does not report which models prevail or specific test results; conclusions depend on the chosen risk metrics, portfolios, and guardrails.
icml-2024-risk-aware-benchmarking-of-lar.tldr: Distribution-aware statistical comparisons can make language-model risk benchmarking more informative than isolated average scores.

icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.problem: Existing theory of in-context learning largely studies single attention layers on linear tasks, leaving learned nonlinear representations less understood.
icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.idea: Analyze a fully connected feature layer followed by linear attention using mean-field dynamics and a separation of training timescales.
icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.results: In the stated limits, the nonconvex parameter-distribution landscape has favorable properties; the analysis shows almost-sure saddle avoidance and derives improvement rates near and away from critical points.
icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.limitations: The guarantees are for a simplified architecture and mean-field, two-timescale limits. The abstract does not establish identical training behavior in finite, multilayer language models.
icml-2024-transformers-learn-nonlinear-f.tldr: A theoretical attention model shows how learning nonlinear features can coexist with favorable optimization dynamics for in-context learning.

icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.problem: Stochastic convex optimizers often need prior knowledge of gradient noise or objective smoothness to choose effective step sizes.
icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.idea: Adapt step sizes using combinations of changes in gradients and iterates, rather than accumulating gradient norms as in AdaGrad.
icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.results: The proposed universal method attains state-of-the-art worst-case rates across the Hölder smoothness class, including nonsmooth and Lipschitz-gradient objectives; an accelerated variant has optimal efficiency guarantees.
icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.limitations: The results concern stochastic convex optimization. The abstract does not present empirical comparisons or extend the guarantees to nonconvex neural-network training.
icml-2024-universal-gradient-methods-for.tldr: A new adaptive step-size rule handles unknown noise and smoothness while retaining strong convex-optimization guarantees.

icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.problem: Training animals on simple component skills before a complex task can transform learning speed, but there is limited theory for deciding when such shaping helps.
icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.idea: Study compositional tasks in a deep policy-gradient model and use statistical-physics tools to derive exact learning dynamics for different training strategies.
icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.results: The analysis finds that shaping benefits depend jointly on task complexity and training protocol, and explains how learning component primitives can make later learning faster and more robust.
icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.limitations: The conclusions come from the analyzed class of compositional tasks. The abstract does not report direct animal experiments or show that the theory covers arbitrary curricula.
icml-2024-why-do-animals-need-shaping-a-.tldr: A tractable reinforcement-learning model explains when practicing task components can accelerate later compositional learning.

icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.problem: Text-generated 3D avatars can suffer from oversaturated textures and poor visual quality, complicating the creation of useful animatable characters.
icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.idea: Generate geometry, texture, and animation in stages, represent avatars through an adaptive training distribution, and tailor score-distillation noise to the avatar.
icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.results: Evaluations report better results than compared text-to-3D and text-to-avatar approaches.
icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.limitations: The abstract does not name evaluation metrics, quantify the gains, or describe animation quality and generation time, so the practical production tradeoffs remain unspecified.
icml-2024-x-oscar-a-progressive-framewor.tldr: A staged geometry-to-texture-to-animation pipeline improves text-guided avatar generation with avatar-specific optimization techniques.

icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.problem: Choosing among language models can save money, but it is unclear when to route a query to one model, escalate through several models, or combine both approaches.
icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.idea: Derive optimal routing and cascading policies within a common framework, then integrate them into cascade routing.
icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.results: The analysis identifies accurate quality estimators as crucial. Experiments report that cascade routing substantially improves the cost–performance tradeoff over the individual strategies.
icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.limitations: The optimality results apply within the paper's model-selection formulation. The abstract does not state the full assumptions, evaluation costs, or numerical gains, and success depends on estimating answer quality well.
icml-2025-a-unified-approach-to-routing-.tldr: A unified policy combines choosing a model with escalating between models to improve language-model cost and quality.

icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.problem: Brain graphs built from pairwise region correlations may not benefit fully from the message-passing operations commonly used by graph neural networks and Transformers.
icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.idea: Replace the usual matrix-product emphasis with a quadratic network motivated by elementwise products, and analyze its relationship to community structure.
icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.results: The proposed Brain Quadratic Network improves performance and efficiency over compared message-passing models; theoretical analysis connects its representations to implicit community detection.
icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.limitations: The motivating analysis concerns brain networks constructed with Pearson correlations. The abstract supplies no numerical gains or evidence that message passing is unnecessary for every type of brain graph.
icml-2025-do-we-really-need-message-pass.tldr: A quadratic network offers an effective alternative to message passing for the studied correlation-based brain networks.

icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.problem: Summarizing a population's opinions into a short slate of statements should preserve proportional representation, even when possible statements cannot be enumerated in advance.
icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.idea: Extend generative social choice to allow imperfect query answers and a budget on total statement length, with language models implementing the queries.
icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.results: The paper provides theoretical guarantees under these extensions and demonstrates representative statement generation with GPT-4o on city-improvement opinions and drug reviews.
icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.limitations: The abstract does not quantify representation quality or specify the assumptions behind the guarantees. Its examples do not establish that generated slates satisfy every practical requirement of a democratic process.
icml-2025-generative-social-choice-the-n.tldr: Generative social choice gains tools for producing representative opinion summaries under length limits and imperfect language-model queries.

icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.problem: Stochastic optimization on curved parameter spaces needs variance-reduction methods with a coherent theory and efficient gradient use.
icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.idea: Unify recursive gradient estimators in Euclidean space, extend them to Riemannian manifolds, and analyze the resulting methods using retractions and vector transport.
icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.results: Two proposed methods match the stated lower bounds on incremental first-order oracle complexity in finite-sum and online settings, and experiments report improvements over existing Riemannian optimizers.
icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.limitations: The guarantees concern the specified nonconvex Riemannian setting and accuracy criterion; the abstract does not detail the assumptions, experimental manifolds, or numerical performance gaps.
icml-2025-serena-a-unified-stochastic-re.tldr: A shared recursive-estimator framework yields theoretically efficient variance-reduced optimization on curved spaces.

icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.problem: Existing model-stealing studies often assume attackers know class names or can handcraft good image-generation prompts, potentially understating risks from less expert attackers.
icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.idea: Study a threat model without that knowledge and introduce an automated system that refines prompts to synthesize useful examples for imitating a queried model.
icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.results: Under equal query budgets, Stealix outperforms compared methods, including methods given class names or detailed prompts, highlighting a model-protection risk from pretrained generative models.
icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.limitations: The abstract does not state model scales, query counts, or replication accuracy. These results describe the evaluated threat model rather than every black-box service.
icml-2025-stealix-model-stealing-via-pro.tldr: Automated prompt refinement can make model imitation effective even without class names or expert-written prompts.

icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.problem: Spiking networks can produce useful variation across time, but existing training methods may provide insufficient diversity in the gradients associated with different time steps.
icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.idea: Rescale logit gradients over time through Temporal Model Calibration to improve temporal heterogeneity and calibration.
icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.results: The method increases temporal gradient diversity and reports state-of-the-art accuracy on ImageNet, DVSCIFAR10, and N-Caltech101.
icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.limitations: The abstract does not give accuracy values, numbers of time steps, or measured energy consumption; the energy motivation for spiking networks is not itself an energy-efficiency result for this method.
icml-2025-training-high-performance-spik.tldr: Adjusting gradients across time improves temporal calibration and classification accuracy in spiking neural networks.

icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.problem: A few labeled anomalies may represent only a small fraction of possible abnormal behavior, making weakly supervised anomaly detection difficult.
icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.idea: Learn normal and anomaly centers with complementary light- and heavy-tailed kernels, preserve within-class diversity through regularization, and share scarce anomaly labels across an ensemble of data partitions.
icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.results: WSAD-DT reports state-of-the-art results on several anomaly-detection benchmarks, outperforming leading ensemble approaches including XGBOD.
icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.limitations: The abstract does not identify the benchmarks, label budgets, or gain sizes, and does not establish detection of anomaly types absent from the evaluated settings.
icml-2025-weakly-supervised-anomaly-dete.tldr: Complementary kernel shapes and an ensemble strategy help make scarce anomaly labels more useful.

icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.problem: CLIP-based systems may share adversarial weaknesses across inputs, domains, tasks, and models, creating risk beyond a single evaluated classifier.
icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.idea: Study a universal perturbation built using a dynamically chosen small set of surrogate models from a larger pool.
icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.results: X-Transfer reports stronger simultaneous transfer across data, domains, models, and tasks than prior universal-perturbation methods, including transfer to downstream vision-language models.
icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.limitations: The abstract does not report perturbation budgets, transfer rates, or the complete model set, so the term universal refers to the evaluated transfer setting rather than all possible systems.
icml-2025-x-transfer-attacks-towards-sup.tldr: A dynamically selected surrogate ensemble exposes broadly transferable adversarial weaknesses in CLIP-based models.

icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.problem: Software assistants need to ask about missing information that affects task success and that a user can realistically supply, without burdening users with unnecessary questions.
icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.idea: Measure information value and answerability using attribution and controlled comparisons, then use those findings as staged reinforcement-learning rewards for an 8B-parameter clarification module.
icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.results: CLARITI matches the reported GPT-5 issue-resolution rate on underspecified tasks while asking 41% fewer questions.
icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.limitations: The study uses simulated users to examine useful responses. The abstract does not provide absolute resolution rates or establish the same question savings with real users in deployment.
icml-2026-asking-what-matters-reward-dri.tldr: Training clarification around relevance and answerability can resolve software tasks with fewer questions.

icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.problem: Published benchmark answers can leak into training or enable leaderboard overfitting, while private evaluation can still leak information through repeated feedback.
icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.idea: Randomly choose one benchmark answer among multiple logically correct alternatives, creating a predictable ceiling on achievable exact-answer accuracy.
icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.results: CapBencher uses scores above that ceiling as a signal of leakage or gaming, with theoretical and empirical validation across benchmarks, models, and training scenarios.
icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.limitations: The interpretation depends on the answer-randomization construction and its accuracy ceiling. The abstract does not give false-alarm rates, detection thresholds, or the kinds of tasks for which multiple correct answers are available.
icml-2026-capbencher-give-your-llm-bench.tldr: A deliberately randomized answer key can give an open benchmark a statistical alarm for test-set overfitting.

icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.problem: Diffusion language models promise parallel generation, but high quality may still require many refinement steps, and continuous-domain acceleration recipes do not transfer directly to discrete tokens.
icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.idea: Train predictions to be consistent in expectation across exact stochastic bridges between noise levels, using a single-stage framework without a pretrained teacher.
icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.results: Consistent Diffusion Language Models outperform strong discrete diffusion baselines and often distilled alternatives on conditional and unconditional generation, with the largest gains at small sampling budgets.
icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.limitations: The abstract does not list benchmark scores, generation times, or compute costs, so quality gains at fewer steps do not alone quantify end-to-end speedups.
icml-2026-consistent-diffusion-language-.tldr: Consistency across discrete noise paths helps diffusion language models generate better text with fewer refinement steps.

icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.problem: Evaluating security-focused code agents requires executable vulnerability tasks, but reproducing them manually is costly and can leave benchmarks behind current software.
icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.idea: Use a multi-agent framework to turn sparse vulnerability records into runnable tasks, then build evaluation and training environments from those reproductions.
icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.results: The authors report 95% solution correctness, 96% environment fidelity, and 66.2% verified success on recent vulnerabilities; a 190-task benchmark supports a fine-tuning study that improves Qwen3-32B from 5.3% to 35.8% on that benchmark.
icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.limitations: The figures measure different evaluation stages and should not be conflated. The abstract does not detail auditing procedures or establish coverage of all vulnerability classes.
icml-2026-cve-factory-scaling-expert-lev.tldr: Automated vulnerability reproduction expands executable security tasks for evaluating and training code agents.

icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.problem: Descriptions of a model's hidden activations may sound informative without actually revealing privileged information about that model's internal computation.
icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.idea: Test whether existing verbalization benchmarks can be solved without activation access and use controlled experiments to distinguish the verbalizer's own knowledge from the target model's knowledge.
icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.results: Strong benchmark performance is possible without target internals, and generated descriptions often reflect the verbalizer's stored knowledge rather than the target's.
icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.limitations: The abstract critiques evaluated methods and datasets rather than proving activation verbalization can never work; it does not provide numerical comparisons or enumerate all controls.
icml-2026-do-activation-verbalization-me.tldr: Activation descriptions need stronger controls because current evaluations can reward information that does not come from the target model's internals.

icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.problem: Fixed tokenization can waste computation or miss meaningful events in sensor signals whose temporal scale and statistical behavior change over time.
icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.idea: Use wavelet-based hierarchical decomposition to identify event boundaries and compress redundant intervals while preserving temporal continuity.
icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.results: Across five sensing datasets, Dywave reports accuracy improvements up to 12%, token-length reductions up to 75%, and improved robustness to domain shifts and changing sequence lengths.
icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.limitations: The abstract does not specify whether the reported accuracy gains are relative or percentage-point changes, and the best-case token reduction need not apply to every dataset or model.
icml-2026-dywave-event-aligned-dynamic-t.tldr: Event-aligned adaptive tokenization makes heterogeneous sensor sequences more compact and useful for prediction.

icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.problem: Group-based reward normalization can become unstable for multimodal reasoning when extreme reward outcomes distort the standard deviation and visual and reasoning errors interact.
icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.idea: Estimate sample difficulty from visual entropy and model confidence, then regroup examples by difficulty and share normalization statistics within those groups.
icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.results: The proposed Durian method reports performance gains across multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks while preserving distinctions among responses within groups.
icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.limitations: The abstract does not identify benchmark scores or ablations, so the separate contributions of the difficulty measures and regrouping are not quantified here.
icml-2026-enhancing-multi-modal-llms-rea.tldr: Difficulty-aware normalization makes reward-based training more stable and effective for the evaluated multimodal reasoning models.

icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.problem: Evolution strategies are often assumed impractical for tuning all the parameters of billion-scale language models, leaving reinforcement learning as the dominant post-training approach.
icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.idea: Apply evolution strategies directly to full-parameter language-model fine-tuning without dimensionality reduction or backpropagation.
icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.results: The experiments report successful billion-parameter tuning and advantages over compared reinforcement-learning implementations in delayed-reward handling, stability, base-model robustness, and resistance to reward hacking.
icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.limitations: The abstract does not report total compute, model-specific scores, or search budgets; its comparisons do not establish that evolution strategies are universally more economical than reinforcement learning.
icml-2026-evolution-strategies-at-scale-.tldr: Billion-scale language models can be fine-tuned with evolution strategies, challenging assumptions about this backpropagation-free approach.

icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.problem: A single embedding geometry may poorly represent dynamic graphs whose local structures vary between hierarchical, grid-like, and cyclic patterns.
icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.idea: Route nodes over time among Transformer experts operating on manifolds with different curvatures, and use a faster Riemannian attention computation.
icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.results: DyGMoCE outperforms compared dynamic-graph methods; its fast attention module reports an average 27.5% speedup and 52.6% memory reduction.
icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.limitations: The abstract does not specify datasets or the baselines for the efficiency figures, and those figures describe the attention module rather than necessarily the entire training pipeline.
icml-2026-fast-mixture-of-curvature-awar.tldr: Curvature-aware experts adapt graph representations to local topology as it changes over time.

icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.problem: A vision-language model can encode spatial relationships internally yet produce a wrong verbal answer, suggesting a gap between representation and output.
icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.idea: Search for geometric counterfactuals during inference and use them to adjust intermediate decoding trajectories and output distributions without updating model parameters.
icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.results: Across the listed image and video benchmarks and multiple model families, GRASP reduces spatial errors and reports accuracy gains up to 26.1% for images and 9.7% for video reasoning.
icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.limitations: The abstract does not specify whether these are relative or percentage-point gains, or report inference overhead; parameter-free adaptation can still require additional computation.
icml-2026-grasp-awakening-latent-spatial.tldr: Inference-time geometric corrections help vision-language models express spatial information already present in their representations.

icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.problem: Mamba can learn new tasks from examples in a prompt, but its nonlinear gating makes the theory of this behavior, especially with outliers, difficult.
icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.idea: Analyze training and generalization of a one-layer model with linear attention followed by a nonlinear gate on new binary-classification tasks.
icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.results: The analysis assigns informative-example selection to attention and outlier suppression to the gate; Mamba can tolerate more outliers than a linear Transformer in the same setting, though convergence may take more iterations.
icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.limitations: The guarantees concern the specified one-layer model, task family, and additive outliers. They do not directly establish robustness for general language prompts or full-scale Mamba systems.
icml-2026-how-can-mamba-learn-in-context.tldr: A simplified Mamba analysis shows how nonlinear gating can trade slower training for stronger in-context resistance to outliers.

icml-2026-latent-thoughts-tuning-bridgin.problem: Continuous latent reasoning can avoid expressing every thought as a token, but repeatedly reusing hidden states may cause unstable representations or feature collapse.
icml-2026-latent-thoughts-tuning-bridgin.idea: Construct latent thoughts by fusing contextual hidden states with predictive guidance from vocabulary embeddings, then train through a three-stage curriculum that supports switching between latent and explicit reasoning.
icml-2026-latent-thoughts-tuning-bridgin.results: LT-Tuning outperforms compared latent-reasoning baselines and reduces feature collapse while retaining strong reasoning accuracy.
icml-2026-latent-thoughts-tuning-bridgin.limitations: The abstract does not identify tasks, numerical gains, or inference savings, so improved latent reasoning quality does not establish a particular compute advantage over explicit reasoning.
icml-2026-latent-thoughts-tuning-bridgin.tldr: Fusing context with vocabulary-based predictive information makes latent-thought training more stable and effective.

icml-2026-local-hessian-spectral-filteri.problem: Estimating the number of locally meaningful data directions becomes difficult in high dimensions because noise from many perpendicular directions can overwhelm the useful signal.
icml-2026-local-hessian-spectral-filteri.idea: Filter the spectrum of the log-density Hessian to separate normal from tangent directions, using stochastic Lanczos quadrature to avoid constructing the full Hessian.
icml-2026-local-hessian-spectral-filteri.results: The proposed estimator scales linearly with ambient dimension and performs robustly on synthetic and real data, with an application to detecting memorization in large diffusion models.
icml-2026-local-hessian-spectral-filteri.limitations: The abstract does not quantify estimation error or specify the density-model assumptions and filtering thresholds, leaving the precise conditions for reliable dimension estimates unspecified.
icml-2026-local-hessian-spectral-filteri.tldr: Spectral filtering makes diffusion-based local dimension estimation more robust to noise in high-dimensional spaces.

icml-2026-mgal-a-multilingual-granularit.problem: Long-context benchmarks often evaluate whole documents in high-resource languages, obscuring failures at different linguistic scales and positions within a document.
icml-2026-mgal-a-multilingual-granularit.idea: Construct tasks from UN reports in six languages, spanning 8K–128K tokens, with word-, sentence-, paragraph-, and document-level questions stratified by location.
icml-2026-mgal-a-multilingual-granularit.results: MGAL finds stronger word-level than coarser-grained performance, an advantage for closed models in lower-resource languages, reliance on superficial cues among similar nearby sentences, and fluent outputs that drift from source facts.
icml-2026-mgal-a-multilingual-granularit.limitations: The benchmark is based on UN reports, so the abstract does not establish that its findings generalize equally to informal, technical, or conversational long contexts.
icml-2026-mgal-a-multilingual-granularit.tldr: A multilingual benchmark reveals how long-context comprehension changes with linguistic granularity and evidence location.

icml-2026-monitorability-as-a-free-gift-.problem: Reward-based training can appear to make reasoning traces easier to monitor, but it is unclear when that improvement occurs or whether traces become more causally faithful.
icml-2026-monitorability-as-a-free-gift-.idea: Evaluate monitorability across model families, training data, and difficulty levels, and analyze the mechanisms associated with changes during training.
icml-2026-monitorability-as-a-free-gift-.results: Gains depend strongly on data diversity and instruction-following examples, do not track capability automatically, and are attributed mainly to sharper response distributions and greater prompt attention rather than increased causal reliance on traces.
icml-2026-monitorability-as-a-free-gift-.limitations: The abstract does not give monitorability metric definitions or effect sizes. The reported improvements therefore should not be equated with universally faithful access to internal computation.
icml-2026-monitorability-as-a-free-gift-.tldr: More capable reasoning after reward training does not automatically mean more transparent or causally faithful reasoning traces.

icml-2026-motimotion-motion-controlled-v.problem: Sparse or imprecise motion instructions can produce implausible videos when a generator follows them rigidly and ignores secondary consequences of movement.
icml-2026-motimotion-motion-controlled-v.idea: Use a vision-language reasoner to refine primary trajectories and propose secondary motions, then vary control strength according to confidence in those plans.
icml-2026-motimotion-motion-controlled-v.results: On the new interaction-focused MotiBench benchmark, automated evaluation and a human study favor MotiMotion's object behavior and interactions over compared approaches.
icml-2026-motimotion-motion-controlled-v.limitations: The abstract does not provide preference percentages, benchmark size, or generation costs, and plausible secondary motion remains a model inference rather than a guarantee of physical correctness.
icml-2026-motimotion-motion-controlled-v.tldr: Reasoning about motion plans before video generation produces more plausible interactions from imperfect trajectory guidance.

icml-2026-online-packet-scheduling-with-.problem: A router must schedule packets before deadlines even though their value may become known only after transmission.
icml-2026-online-packet-scheduling-with-.idea: Model scheduling as a bandit-feedback problem with stochastic packet values and derive algorithms for different deadline slackness and randomization regimes.
icml-2026-online-packet-scheduling-with-.results: The algorithms achieve alpha-regret of order square root of KT up to logarithmic factors. For short-deadline instances with finitely many packet types, the deterministic competitive ratio improves on the stated golden-ratio barrier.
icml-2026-online-packet-scheduling-with-.limitations: The bounds depend on the stochastic-value model and scheduling regime; the abstract does not report network experiments or establish the same results for arbitrary adversarial packet values.
icml-2026-online-packet-scheduling-with-.tldr: Learning packet values can be combined with deadline-aware scheduling while retaining strong regret and competitive-ratio guarantees.

icml-2026-rooted-absorbed-prefix-traject.problem: GFlowNet-based language-model tuning can collapse onto similar prefixes and biased lengths when early decisions receive weak feedback and replay examples are unrepresentative.
icml-2026-rooted-absorbed-prefix-traject.idea: Propagate terminal reward back to intermediate prefixes through a root-anchored objective, and refresh replay data with a submodular strategy balancing reward and diversity.
icml-2026-rooted-absorbed-prefix-traject.results: On tasks including molecule generation through SMILES strings, the combined approach improves optimization and molecular diversity while maintaining high validity.
icml-2026-rooted-absorbed-prefix-traject.limitations: The abstract does not quantify diversity or reward gains and does not establish that valid generated molecules are experimentally useful or that the improvements cover all language-generation tasks.
icml-2026-rooted-absorbed-prefix-traject.tldr: Stronger prefix supervision and more diverse replay reduce collapse in the evaluated GFlowNet generation tasks.

icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.problem: A spoken-dialogue model can benefit from preparing a response while the user is still speaking, rather than starting a separate reasoning stage afterward.
icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.idea: Recursively carry latent embeddings forward during speech perception and train the process with an evidence-lower-bound objective that avoids explicit reasoning annotations.
icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.results: FLAIR reports competitive speech-benchmark and full-duplex interaction results while its causal think-while-listening design avoids an additional post-listening reasoning stage.
icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.limitations: The abstract does not give latency measurements, hardware costs, or benchmark scores; its latency claim concerns the concurrent design rather than a detailed end-to-end deployment profile.
icml-2026-the-silent-thought-modeling-in.tldr: Latent reasoning performed during listening helps a full-duplex speech model prepare responses without a separate reasoning pause.

icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.problem: Federated adversarial training has convergence analyses, but these do not by themselves explain whether robustness learned across clients generalizes to unseen examples.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.idea: Analyze algorithmic stability for stochastic-gradient methods, then study Moreau-envelope optimization and gradient-free variants.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.results: The framework derives perturbation-dependent generalization bounds, shows that stronger attacks can worsen them, and obtains a perturbation-independent bound with the proposed optimization approach; analysis also covers a black-box setting.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.limitations: The abstract does not enumerate the stability assumptions or provide empirical gains. A bound independent of perturbation strength does not mean arbitrary attacks cannot affect actual performance.
icml-2026-towards-understanding-generali.tldr: Stability analysis links federated adversarial training choices to generalization and motivates smoother optimization alternatives.

icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.problem: A few extreme weights or activations can stretch quantization ranges and increase error when language models are represented with very few bits.
icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.idea: Combine a Hadamard transform with data-dependent second moments to obtain an efficient non-orthogonal block transform for joint weight and activation quantization.
icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.results: WUSH has near-optimality guarantees under stated assumptions and reports four-bit accuracy gains of 2.8 average points with round-to-nearest and 0.7 with GPTQ on a cited Llama configuration, plus up to 5.8× per-layer throughput over BF16.
icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.limitations: The optimum is tied to specified block quantizers and assumptions. Per-layer peak throughput does not establish the same whole-model speedup.
icml-2026-wush-near-optimal-adaptive-tra.tldr: A data-adaptive transform reduces outlier-driven errors in low-bit language-model quantization.

neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.problem: Annealing-based constraint networks need to escape poor configurations without disturbing parts that already satisfy constraints, yet an externally chosen temperature schedule treats progress globally.
neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.idea: Let each unit set its own temperature at every update, allowing poorly satisfied regions to keep changing while stable regions remain settled.
neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.results: The abstract reports faster and more consistent discovery of global maxima than externally scheduled systems and describes the implementation as computationally simple.
neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.limitations: The source abstract contains transcription errors and no numerical comparisons or formal convergence guarantee; its performance claim should not be read as proof of global optimization for every network.
neurips-1988-automatic-local-annealing-e.tldr: Locally chosen annealing temperatures let difficult parts of a constraint network keep searching while good parts stabilize.

neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.problem: Large input patterns can require many network parameters, while a fixed training corpus may not support learning that many degrees of freedom reliably.
neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.idea: Discuss dimensionality reduction and the use of prior knowledge as ways to control model complexity in an isolated-word recognition task.
neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.results: The abstract identifies the application and methodological focus but gives no experimental scores or comparison establishing which technique works best.
neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.limitations: The available abstract is brief and does not describe the individual techniques, dataset, or measured outcomes, so a more detailed algorithmic or performance claim would require the paper.
neurips-1989-dimensionality-reduction-an.tldr: Reducing input dimensionality and incorporating prior knowledge are explored as ways to make word-recognition networks fit limited data.

neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.problem: A trained neural system may experience faults in its learned weights, and different fault types may affect performance differently.
neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.idea: Examine Albus' CMAC network after training, comparing lost weights with weights forced to saturated values while varying the network's generalization setting.
neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.results: Greater generalization reduces sensitivity to lost-weight faults but increases sensitivity to saturated-weight faults.
neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.limitations: The abstract does not define the generalization parameter, fault rates, or task metrics. Its opposing trends concern these two fault types in CMAC networks, not neural-network robustness in general.
neurips-1989-operational-fault-tolerance.tldr: In CMAC networks, a setting that protects against missing weights can increase vulnerability to saturated weights.

neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.problem: An arm with opposing muscles has multiple ways to produce the same joint torque, making it difficult to learn commands that control motion and contact force together.
neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.idea: Combine feedback-error learning with a parallel hierarchical neural controller and two pseudoinverse-based control laws favoring small changes in muscle tension or motor commands.
neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.results: The formulation resolves the stated inverse-control ambiguity, and experiments with an artificial muscle arm plus simulations demonstrate the controller's effectiveness.
neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.limitations: The abstract gives no tracking-error values, force-control accuracy, or robustness tests, so its demonstration does not establish performance for other robot designs or disturbances.
neurips-1990-learning-trajectory-and-for.tldr: A hierarchical neural controller uses structured control laws to learn simultaneous movement and force control in a redundant muscle-driven arm.

neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.problem: Understanding speech production requires connecting muscle commands to the movements of speech articulators rather than modeling speech only as an acoustic sequence.
neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.idea: Train a neural forward-dynamics model from physiological movement and muscle-activity recordings, probe it with simulated perturbations, and use a cascaded network to generate continuous commands from discrete targets.
neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.results: The learned model supports assessment of natural frequency, damping, and coupling between articulators, and the cascade generates continuous motor-command trajectories.
neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.limitations: The abstract does not report prediction errors, the amount of physiological data, or comparisons to biological perturbation responses; modeled dynamics should not be assumed fully validated by the description alone.
neurips-1991-forward-dynamics-modeling-o.tldr: Physiological recordings train neural models that connect speech-muscle commands, articulator motion, and continuous motor control.

neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.problem: Ordinary gradient-based learning can encounter difficulties when network activations or error functions are nonsmooth, including piecewise-linear transfer functions.
neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.idea: Apply results from nonsmooth optimization to design a learning algorithm for networks with these components.
neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.results: The paper presents an algorithm and motivates it with claimed advantages of an alternative error norm over the usual squared-error-style choice.
neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.limitations: The supplied abstract has corrupted mathematical notation for the norms and does not report numerical results; their exact definitions and the claimed advantage require checking the full paper.
neurips-1991-learning-in-feedforward-net.tldr: Nonsmooth optimization provides a principled route to training networks whose functions do not have ordinary derivatives everywhere.

neurips-1991-learning-to-make-coherent-p.problem: Learning depth by assuming nearby visual locations agree can fail at surface boundaries, where interpolation across an edge mixes unrelated depths.
neurips-1991-learning-to-make-coherent-p.idea: Extend an unsupervised coherence-learning approach with either rejection of discontinuities or a mixture of specialized asymmetric interpolators that avoid crossing them.
